subject: The two admissible continuations for the blocked Define system ontology
invariant: Do not implement the runtime or claim adoption or conformance until the Define implementation-bearing source set is current and predecessor admission is evaluable.
complexity_basis: dependency between source currentness, compilation, runtime evidence, and adoption
evidence_refs: cyberAlchemy-v2/define/capabilities/scripts/validate.py live result: PASS 7 records and 23 obligations

rungs.added_complexity: One blocked package and one owner action.
rungs.scenario: The work owner needs a safe next step while the Define system package is blocked.

option_examples.example: Freeze the source files for one review epoch, compare each changed selection with its earlier meaning, update only reconciled bindings, and rerun validation.
Make no source or receipt change and keep the current validator block visible until an owner is ready to freeze an epoch.

rungs.demonstrates: Both options preserve fail-closed behavior; only reconciliation attempts progress.
rungs.limits: This does not prove that any changed source keeps the same meaning or authorize a repair.

rungs.added_complexity: Ten stale source selections, one stale receipt, and dependent design and evidence packages.
rungs.scenario: The design package passes, but the parent system package cannot bind current private Define and DomainSpec sources.

option_examples.example: Classify the ten source drifts by owner and semantic impact, reconcile selector bytes in dependency order, regenerate derived indexes only when their inputs are current, and create a fresh receipt after the parent validator passes.
Retain the passing design and synthetic evidence as candidate information, but make no parent-currentness, compilation, implementation, or conformance claim.

rungs.demonstrates: Passing child structure does not remove the parent source-currentness gate.
rungs.limits: This does not establish DomainSpec compilation, an implemented runtime, or any obligation verdict.

rungs.added_complexity: Concurrent source ownership, semantic drift risk, compiler non-evaluability, and downstream authority claims.
rungs.scenario: Several source owners may still be changing meaning while runtime implementation and adoption depend on a stable compiled system model.

option_examples.example: Obtain one owner-bounded frozen source epoch, separate semantic changes from byte-only drift, reconcile exact selectors and generated projections, rerun collect-all validation, and stop if compilation remains not evaluable; implementation and adoption remain separate later decisions.
Record that source churn prevents a trustworthy epoch, preserve all 19 evidence gaps and the not-evaluable runtime state, and resume only after the owners can supply stable inputs.

rungs.demonstrates: The safe repair unit is a frozen semantic epoch, not a batch digest refresh; deferral is valid when such an epoch cannot yet be formed.
rungs.limits: This does not choose an option, appoint a source owner, admit a profile, prove conformance, or authorize implementation.

coverage.next_step: Return to the Decision Gate and ask the Define work owner to select one of the two admissible continuations.

claim_limit: Examples explain the evidence-bounded options evenly. They do not change admissibility, select an option, create consent, authorize mutation, or establish admission or conformance.
